contracts.definition: Inspects, sets, clears and toggles selected integer bits while preserving unrelated bits.
common_misconceptions: Boolean conjunction inspects the same state as an integer mask.
Clearing selected bits may also reset unrelated flags.
XOR is interchangeable with setting bits already present.
mastery: Expresses each mask operation with explicit integer types.
Checks both selected-bit behavior and preservation of other bits.

observable_outcomes: Checks whether any or all selected bits are present, including zero-mask behavior fixed by the task contract.
Sets, clears, and toggles selected bits and preserves every unrelated bit for overlapping, disjoint, zero, and already-set masks.

contracts.minimum_rationale: Three primary encounters reserve distinct learner-authored implementation, repair, and tests of an existing implementation; two further encounters apply the same outcome with materially different contracts. This retains the ordinary 3/5 foundation tier; availability/depth minima are not mandatory linear completions.

forms.implementation: Implement mask inspection and transformation for supplied fixed-width masks.
forms.debugging: Repair a transformation that confuses set and toggle or erases unrelated bits.
forms.verification-or-integration: Write tests distinguishing any/all inspection, zero masks, pre-existing selected bits, and preservation of unrelated flags.

contracts.definition: Reasons about integer shift direction, count, operand type and width for constant and runtime operands.
common_misconceptions: A runtime shift count is automatically reduced modulo the operand width.
Signed and unsigned right shifts always fill the same high bits.
An untyped constant and a fixed-width integer always retain the same shifted value.
mastery: Chooses operand types and valid count domains explicitly.
Separates constant representability from runtime fixed-width shift behavior.

observable_outcomes: Separates untyped/typed constant representability from fixed-width runtime left-shift bit loss.
Handles count zero, width and beyond-width counts without assuming modulo reduction; distinguishes signed and unsigned right shifts.
Distinguishes invalid negative constant counts from the runtime panic for a negative signed count. Compile-negative examples are checker-owned semantic facts, never mutant kills.

contracts.minimum_rationale: Three primary encounters reserve distinct learner-authored implementation, repair, and tests of an existing implementation; two further encounters apply the same outcome with materially different contracts. This retains the ordinary 3/5 foundation tier; availability/depth minima are not mandatory linear completions.

forms.implementation: Compute a finite table of fixed-width runtime shift results and explicitly stated invalid-count behavior.
forms.debugging: Repair width-modulo, conversion-order or signed-fill defects in a normally compiling implementation.
forms.verification-or-integration: Write tests for fixed-width boundaries, signed/unsigned behavior, and runtime negative-count policy, with compiler facts checked separately.

contracts.definition: Defines finite recursive decomposition with correct base cases, progressing subproblems and complete result combination.
common_misconceptions: A terminal branch guarantees termination even when a recursive subproblem does not progress.
One recursive branch is sufficient when the decomposition requires multiple subproblems.
Correct output or an unused recursive call proves that recursion performed the requested computation.
mastery: States a decreasing measure and handles its terminal inputs.
Combines every required recursive subresult without duplicating or skipping branches.

observable_outcomes: Handles terminal and minimal nonterminal inputs, plus unequal branches when the task decomposition branches.
For implementation and debugging evidence, executes learner-authored recursive decomposition that progresses to terminal cases and contributes required results.
For verification evidence, learner-authored tests distinguish missing base cases, nonprogressing or skipped branches, and incorrect combination; this alone does not prove authored recursion.

contracts.minimum_rationale: Three primary encounters reserve distinct learner-authored implementation, repair, and tests of an existing implementation; two further encounters apply the same outcome with materially different contracts. This retains the ordinary 3/5 foundation tier; availability/depth minima are not mandatory linear completions.

forms.implementation: Author recursive decomposition and result combination under an explicit decreasing measure.
forms.debugging: Repair progress, terminal handling, or branch combination in an existing recursive implementation.
forms.verification-or-integration: Write tests for an existing recursive API that expose base-case and decomposition defects; separate implementation evidence still required.

assessment_gate.rule: No P25 or recursion implementation/debugging task authoring/promotion until a bounded public verification contract and disposable proof reject iterative substitution, dead self-calls and unused dummy recursion, while accepting the stated direct/helper/mutual forms. Output tests plus selfcall AST presence are insufficient.
proof_requirements: Iterative, dead and dummy recursive substitutes fail a useful public assertion
Behavioral base/progress/branch/combination mutants compile and fail public tests
Restrictions and accepted recursive forms are stated to learner; no hidden implementation shape
